pull.title: fuzz: Cover block filter P2P messages
pull.body:
The BIP157 P2P messages are not covered by any fuzz targets at all.

Fix this to cover them via the P2P targets.

Should be possible to test by verifying the integer sanitizer is triggered (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36321#issuecomment-5810977529):

```
$ echo 'FwAAAAEAAABcX2dldGNmY2hlY2twdAAftOvdD0sFqXEx6US5VIknlsOJqZ5goMwtmwZBPdCxQVxf
AfkGKP39/f0v/Q/9E1AP/f2ybAT1Af39A/399wEAuXEAAAAAAAAAAAB1z3QAbgAAQAHm/f39/f39
/f39/S8/D/0B/f3IAAcBBWNmaf8DAAAA' | base64 --decode > /tmp/msg.bin

$ UBSAN_OPTIONS="suppressions=$(pwd)/test/sanitizer_suppressions/ubsan:print_stacktrace=0:halt_on_error=0:report_error_type=1" FUZZ=process_messages ./bld-cmake/bin/fuzz /tmp/msg.bin 

./bld-cmake/bin/fuzz: Running 1 inputs 1 time(s) each.
/src/net_processing.cpp:3662:33: runtime error: unsigned integer overflow: 0 - 1 cannot be represented in type 'size_type' (aka 'unsigned long')
/src/net_processing.cpp:3662:18: runtime error: implicit conversion from type 'size_type' (aka 'unsigned long') of value 18446744073709551615 (64-bit, unsigned) to type 'int' changed the value to -1 (32-bit, signed)

test: DestroyAllBlockFilterIndexes in ~ChainTestingSetup()

DestroyAllBlockFilterIndexes is a no-op when no indexes exist, but
calling it here avoids a use-after-free: The validation signals are
destructed in ~ChainTestingSetup, so there is a UAF when
BaseIndex::~BaseIndex() later calls Stop(), and Stop() dereferences
m_chain->context()->validation_signals.

The shutdown order follows the one in init.cpp:
DestroyAllBlockFilterIndexes() after FlushBackgroundCallbacks().

comments.body: Can you explain why it deadlocks? I couldn't figure this bit out

Sure. I guess the "fuzzed block" explanation is a bit confusing, because this is a general unit test utility, not limited to fuzzing.

The idea is:

* block connection events happens under cs_main: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/3b9768a07aee6851de24f9c23bcdeeac2d872d23/src/validation.cpp#L3367-L3408
* With `ImmediateBackgroundTaskRunner` a new thread is spawned to handle it, which obviously can't take cs_main again.
* Thus, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/3b9768a07aee6851de24f9c23bcdeeac2d872d23/src/kernel/chain.cpp#L25 will deadlock via callback thread: BaseIndex::BlockConnected() → ProcessBlock() → kernel::MakeBlockInfo() → tries to lock cs_main


I guess in theory one could use `ImmediateTaskRunner` (reverting https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36046), but that would bring back the issues from there.

> I think CI failures are because in process_message(s) the `static testing_setup` is destructed before `static g_filter_indexes` so `BaseIndex::Stop` will try to access `testing_setup.m_node`.

Thx, fixed by destroying the indexes in the testing dtor, which seems useful generally, unrelated to the changes here.
